title: The Impact of Pre- and Post-Processing Processes on Corrosion Resistance of MAO Coatings on Mg and Its Alloys: A Systematic Review
content: Mg alloys, renowned for their lightweight and exceptional mechanical properties, hold promise for widespread applications in aerospace, automotive manufacturing, and biomedical fields. However, their limited corrosion resistance has hindered their practical usage. MAO (MAO) technology serves as an effective coating method to enhance the corrosion resistance of Mg alloys, yet the inherent porosity of MAO coatings remains a performance bottleneck. To optimize coating performance, pre-processing and post-processing have emerged as research hotspots. pre-processing regulates the surface state thereby promoting uniform growth of the MAO coating, while post-processing further reduces coating porosity and enhances corrosion resistance. This paper comprehensively reviews the impact of various pre-processing and post-processing methods, such as shot peening pre-processing and immersion post-processing, on the microstructure, composition, and performance of Mg alloy MAO coatings. Utilizing electrochemical testing and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) characterization techniques, the paper reveals the crucial role of pre-processing in optimizing interfacial bonding and post-processing in enhancing coating density.Finally, the paper concludes with a prospect on the development of pre-processing and post-processing techniques.
